textoCompleto:
qSOFA Scale

QUICK SEPSIS TRIAGE

The qSOFA (quick SOFA) is a rapid screening tool to identify patients with suspected infection at imminent risk of sepsis and unfavorable outcomes.
Patient Data

Fill in for Medical Record/PDF Report

Screening Criteria
Final qSOFA Score

Assessment Memory

Exemplifying with NANDA: NANDA diagnoses related to the identified problems (Educational purpose)
Based on respiratory, hemodynamic, and neurological dysfunction.

Processing clinical reasoning...

A NANDA diagnosis requires a careful evaluation of its taxonomies and the search for defining characteristics and related factors. The disclosure of diagnoses on this scale serves only an educational purpose, to promote its use and help users become familiar with the various diagnoses. Under no circumstances should it induce the user to indiscriminately apply any nursing diagnosis without the support of clinical findings obtained through history taking, physical examination, and other systematic tools that will guide the nurse in prescribing care.

Frequently Asked Questions
Follow more nursing information on our nursing forum.

Related Scales
NEWS Scale National Early Warning Score System.

MEWS Scale Modified Early Warning Score System.

Glasgow Scale Assessment of level of consciousness.

Scientific Reference
SINGER, M. et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA , v. 315, n. 8, p. 801-810, 2016.

Score Interpretation

Low Risk (0-1 point)
Reduced risk of unfavorable outcomes at this time. Maintain clinical monitoring.

High Risk (2-3 points)
High risk of sepsis. Consider additional assessment, rapid intervention, and laboratory tests.
